title: dedicated-autoscaler-add-backpressure-and-utilization-reporting-enhancement
author: Aisha Chen
description: Motivation: customer fleets saw intermittent latency spikes under bursty traffic leading to degraded p99s and failed SLAs. This PR implements conservative backpressure at the dedicated-autoscaler level and expands utilization reporting so operators can observe effective throughput, queue lengths, and backpressure events over time. Summary of changes: 1) Add backpressure tokenbucket gating and soft-shed path for overloaded pools. 2) Surface per-fleet and per-priority utilization metrics (utilization_pct, queued_requests, backpressure_events, tokens_dropped) to the telemetry pipeline. 3) Instrument autoscaler controller with end-to-end latency buckets and queue time histograms. 4) Add config knobs (burst_capacity, burst_window_s, backpressure_threshold_pct, smoothing_alpha) with sensible defaults and backwards-compatible behavior. Rollout plan: feature gated behind a runtime flag (autoscaler.backpressure.enabled) defaulting to false for 2 weeks, staged rollout to dedicated fleets in prod, with automatic rollback on error budget violation. Testing: unit tests for tokenbucket math and smoothing, integration test that simulates burst load and validates degradation path, e2e canary on a subset of fleets. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked - ENG-4982 - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] CI green on linux/macos - [x] Telemetry dashboards added - [x] Migration plan documented Changes in this PR are additive and opt-in via the runtime flag. No schema-breaking changes to public API or DB.

release_notes: Add optional autoscaler backpressure and improved utilization reporting for Dedicated fleets. Feature is opt-in via autoscaler.backpressure.enabled and ships with dashboards and runbook. Improves stability under bursty traffic by enabling soft-shed and tokenbucket gating.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover tokenbucket refill, smoothing and edge-cases. Integration test validates that backpressure prevents oversubscription and triggers soft-shed. Canary run on 3 fleets for 48h validated no SLA regressions on low-traffic periods and <2% p99 improvement under sustained bursts.
notes: This PR was intentionally conservative: backpressure is opt-in and metrics are additive. Next follow-ups: adaptive burst_capacity tuning based on historical traffic and per-fleet model-specific defaults.
migration_impact: None to public API. Operators must enable runtime flag to activate behavior. Dashboards updated; no migration scripts required.
